Q: How to find the ExternalVersionId for App Pinning in an MDM A:

You don't get the externalVersionId from Xcode or App Store Connect directly. It is an App Store identifier assigned to a specific App Store version.

If you are the app developer and don't have an MDM, you can retrieve it from Apple's App Store metadata rather than using an MDM.

For example, Apple's legacy metadata lookup response contains the value as:

"version": {
    "display": "5.0.1",
    "externalId": 830786363
}

That externalId is the value used as the EVID / ExternalVersionIdentifier.

The important part is that the EVID is not the same as your CFBundleVersion or App Store version string. Also, Apple notes that EVIDs can differ by storefront/region and device type, so make sure you query the correct storefront and platform.

If you're implementing this for an MDM, the other option is to send an InstalledApplicationList command requesting ExternalVersionIdentifier; the device will return the EVID for the installed App Store version.

So, as an app developer, you don't necessarily need to purchase an MDM just to obtain the value. You can query Apple's App Store metadata for the app/version, provided you use the appropriate Apple API/access method.

Q: Starting apache/kafka container in Kraft mode throws error in /etc/kafka/docker/configure !1: unbound variable A:

I had a similar issue today. Adding

KAFKA_OPTS: "-Djava.security.auth.login.config=/etc/kafka/kafka_server_jaas.conf"

to the environment variables, along with mounting the kafka_server_jaas.conf file, did the trick.
It appears that the script /etc/kafka/docker/configure throws the error unless the KAFKA_OPTS variable is explicitly set.
I used https://www.baeldung.com/kafka-authentication-sasl-plain as a configuration reference.

Q: Missing overlay ("Draw over other apps") permission window on Android 10 Go devices, such as Wiko Y61 A:

The overlay/"Display over other apps" permission is disabled on Android Go device as of Android 10 for, as the message notes, performance reasons. There is an exception for apps that were installed and received the permission before the device was upgraded to Android 10, but otherwise, there is no way for apps to receive that permission.

If you need to lock down a device, you should look at the APIs for managing dedicated enterprise devices. Normal Android apps are otherwise generally restricted from doing things that could lock down a device, as that capability is also quite useful for malware seeking to take over a device. You're better off using the APIs that were intended for this, as hacky workarounds in this area are likely to be broken in the future (see, for instance, other restrictions being imposed on the overlay permission).

Q: Iphone Ipad QA testing process A:

You don't necessarily need to own every iPhone and every version of iOS.

For older iOS versions, you can use the iOS Simulator in Xcode if that SDK/simulator runtime is installed. You can also test on a few real devices to catch issues that the simulator doesn't reproduce.

In practice, I'd recommend:

  • Test on the oldest iOS version you support.

  • Test on the newest iOS version.

  • Test on the main screen sizes/device types you support.

  • Use real devices for final testing, especially for UI, performance, and device-specific problems.

  • Use the simulator for quickly testing different OS versions and screen sizes.

You can install additional simulator runtimes when Apple provides them, but you generally won't have every historical iOS/device combination available in every Xcode version.

Q: git ignore everything with "secret" in path or filename A:

Just add both entries as:

**/*secret*
**/*secret*/**

Q: Python file delimited with double tabs A:

How much do you know about your data? Is it ever possible that an entry contains a double-tab? If not, I'd abandon the csv module and use the simple approach:

with open('data.csv') as data:
    for line in data:
        print line.strip().split('\t\t')

The csv module is nice for doing tricky things, like determining when a delimiter should split a string, and when it shouldn't because it is part of an entry. For example, say we used spaces as delimiters, and we had a row such as:

"this" "is" "a test"

We surround each entry with quotes, giving three entries. Clearly, if we use the approach of splitting on spaces, we'll get

['"this"', '"is"', '"a', 'test"']

which is not what we want. The csv module is useful here. But if we can guarantee that whenever a space shows up, it is a delimiter, then there's no need to use the power of the csv module. Just use str.split and call it a day.
